gap.summary: The homebound field on the 10/01/2026 home health order is left unchecked with no supporting clinical findings, and no other practitioner statement certifies homebound status.
gap.what_would_satisfy: A signed statement from the treating physician that the member is homebound, with the supporting clinical findings, such as the walker-dependent mobility, the need for standby assistance and the hip precautions.
gap.suggested_action: Ask Dr. Daniel K. Abernathy's office whether he can complete the homebound section of the 10/01/2026 face-to-face and home health order, if it reflects his clinical judgment. Any addendum must be dated and signed by him.

bases.title: Home-based care in place of a facility admission

requirements.text: Member meets Plan criteria for SNF or inpatient rehabilitation admission, documented by physician or case manager.
requirements.policy_text: The member meets Plan criteria for admission to a skilled nursing facility or an inpatient rehabilitation facility, as documented by the treating physician or a case manager.

evidence.quote: Patient meets Alderpoint criteria for skilled nursing facility admission: she requires daily skilled nursing and skilled physical therapy 5 times per week after hip hemiarthroplasty.

key_phrases.text: meets Alderpoint criteria for skilled nursing facility admission
she requires daily skilled nursing and skilled physical therapy 5 times per week

evidence.rationale: The case manager explicitly documents that the patient meets the Plan's criteria for skilled nursing facility admission, and states the skilled needs behind that.

near_misses.quote: Physical therapy 5 times per week in a facility, or 3 times per week at home if a trained caregiver is present.
near_misses.why_not: The physical therapist offers facility or home therapy as alternatives and does not state that Plan admission criteria are met.

near_misses.quote: The patient and her daughter decline skilled nursing facility placement and ask for discharge home with home health services.
near_misses.why_not: This records the patient's and family's placement preference, not whether the admission criteria are met.

near_misses.quote: Home with home health services (skilled nursing and physical therapy).
near_misses.why_not: This is the discharge disposition actually chosen and says nothing about whether facility admission criteria are met.

requirements.text: Home evaluated as appropriate and safe, including caregiver availability if needed.
requirements.policy_text: The home setting was evaluated and found clinically appropriate and safe for the ordered services, including caregiver availability when a caregiver is needed.

evidence.quote: The home setting is clinically appropriate and safe for discharge with home health nursing and physical therapy.

key_phrases.text: home setting is clinically appropriate and safe

evidence.rationale: The occupational therapist's pre-discharge home visit explicitly concludes the home setting is clinically appropriate and safe for the ordered home health services.

evidence.quote: Her daughter, Anna Kowalczyk, lives with the patient, is available 24 hours a day for the first 6 weeks, and completed transfer and injection training on 10/01/2026.

key_phrases.text: is available 24 hours a day for the first 6 weeks

evidence.rationale: The case manager documents that a named caregiver lives with the patient, is available around the clock for the first 6 weeks, and has completed training.

near_misses.quote: Physical therapy 5 times per week in a facility, or 3 times per week at home if a trained caregiver is present.
near_misses.why_not: This is a conditional therapy recommendation that makes home care depend on a trained caregiver; it does not document that a caregiver is available or that the home was evaluated.

near_misses.quote: Lives with her daughter in a single-story house.
near_misses.why_not: This is background from the inpatient PT evaluation on living situation; it is not a home safety evaluation and says nothing about the daughter's availability.

near_misses.quote: She walks to the bathroom and kitchen with the walker while her daughter stands by.
near_misses.why_not: This is a post-discharge telephone report of the daughter assisting; it is not a clinician's evaluation of the home or of caregiver availability.

requirements.text: Expected home health cost does not exceed expected facility-based cost.
requirements.policy_text: The expected cost of the home health services does not exceed the expected cost of the facility-based alternative.

blocks.text: Re: Appeal of denial dated 2026-10-05, Case B-3117, Alderpoint Health Plan, home health skilled nursing and physical therapy

We request reconsideration of this denial. This appeal is based on the plan provision for home-based care in place of a facility admission, and the record excerpts below are offered under that provision.

The record documents that the patient meets Alderpoint criteria for skilled nursing facility admission, as she requires daily skilled nursing and skilled physical therapy 5 times per week after hip hemiarthroplasty.
The record documents that the home setting is clinically appropriate and safe for discharge with home health nursing and physical therapy.
The record documents that the patient's daughter, Anna Kowalczyk, lives with her, is available 24 hours a day for the first 6 weeks, and completed transfer and injection training on 10/01/2026.

The record documents expected costs at Plan contracted rates of $10,400 for 20 days in a skilled nursing facility at $520 per day, compared with $4,350 for 30 home health visits at $145 per visit, and identifies home health as the lower-cost option.
The record documents a physician order for skilled nursing 2 visits per week for 6 weeks (12 visits) and physical therapy 3 visits per week for 6 weeks (18 visits).
The record documents an encounter on 10/01/2026 that was related to the primary reason for home health, which is care after right hip hemiarthroplasty.

The record documents that skilled nursing is needed for surgical incision assessment, enoxaparin injection teaching and monitoring, and pain medication management, and that skilled physical therapy is needed for gait training, transfer training, hip precaution teaching, and progressive strengthening.
Thank you for your review. Please contact our office if any additional information would be helpful.
